Your footage. Your brief. Your call.

### Your taste. The final cut.
See the workflow

#### Review every Short
Fine-tune clip timing and framing in a native desktop editor before exporting.

#### Ask for an edit
Use editor chat to request changes in plain language, from trimming to muting the audio.

#### Keep your originals
Source files are copied, never modified. New batches append, and each batch can be undone.

#### Ready to share
Export vertical MP4s at up to 1080 × 1920, then upload them to your favorite platforms.

BETA ACCESS

# Start creating.
Prism is in beta. Sign in to try it, and check Settings in the app for your AI usage allowance. Paid plans are not available yet.

ABOUT THE BETA

### Good to know.

**How does beta access work?**
Sign in to try Prism. AI usage limits apply; check Settings in the app for your allowance. Paid plans are not available yet.

**Which platforms does Prism run on?**
The beta is available for macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. Windows and Linux ports have not yet been tested on real devices.

**Which languages do captions support?**
Prism transcribes speech and writes captions in the language spoken in your video. Automatic filler-word cleanup currently works for English only.

URL: https://prismclips.app/faq
Title: Help & FAQs — Prism

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

# A little clarity. Then, create.
Everything to know before your first Short.

**How much does Prism cost?**
Prism is in beta and paid plans are not available yet. AI usage limits apply; check Settings in the app for your allowance. About beta access.

**What happens to my footage?**
Your source files, projects, preview, and rendering stay on your computer. Audio chunks, transcripts, sampled frames, and editor chat messages are sent for AI processing. On Mac, they go through Prism’s server and OpenRouter to an AI model; on Windows and Linux, they go to Google Gemini. Prism needs an internet connection; it has no offline AI mode.

**Can I change the Shorts Prism picks?**
Yes. Review and adjust every Short before export. Change the timing, choose Fill, Fit, or Split framing, try seven caption styles, or ask the editor chat to help with edits.

**Where can I post my exports?**
Prism exports vertical MP4 files at up to 1080 × 1920. Upload them yourself to your favorite short-form platforms, including YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and TikTok. Direct publishing isn’t built in.

**Is this ready for my daily workflow?**
Prism is an early beta. The Mac pipeline works end to end, but you should review every clip and expect rough edges. Windows and Linux ports are available but still need verification on real devices. Read the current limits.

**Do I need a Prism account?**
On Mac, sign in to the app with your Prism account to use the AI service. Your dashboard also shows your export stats and history. Windows and Linux use your own Gemini API key instead. Create an account.

**How do I get started?**
Download Prism, sign in on Mac or add your Gemini API key on Windows or Linux, and import a video. See the three-step workflow for a quick tour.

### Something else on your mind?
Check the project documentation ↗ or share your feedback on GitHub ↗.

URL: https://prismclips.app/about
Title: About — Prism

ABOUT PRISM

# One video in. Many Shorts out.
Prism is a desktop app that turns long videos into vertical Shorts with captions.

### What Prism does
Import a podcast, lecture, interview or stream. Prism transcribes it, finds moments that stand on their own, and cuts them into vertical Shorts. It reframes each one for the small screen and adds captions in the language spoken in your video. You review every Short and make the final cut before you export.

### Who it’s for
Creators, podcasters and streamers who want more short-form videos from the long recordings they already make, without spending hours in an editor.

### Where it runs
Prism is an early beta for macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. Windows and Linux ports have not yet been tested on real devices. Your source files and finished videos stay on your machine. See Privacy for what is sent for AI processing.

### Beta access
Sign in to try Prism during the beta. AI usage limits apply; check Settings in the app for your allowance. About beta access.

### Learn more
See features, how it works and the FAQs, or download Prism.

### v0.2.0-beta.2
2026-10-21 · BETA

#### New

- Installers for macOS (.dmg), Windows (.exe) and Linux (.AppImage), built on every release tag.

- Native Windows and Linux workspaces on a shared engine. Both are untested on real devices.

#### Fixed

- Gemini timeouts now fail the run instead of silently dropping results.

- Crops stay inside frames with odd pixel sizes.

- macOS release builds with the newest Xcode and its own SQLite.

### Earlier builds
2026-10-18 – 10-20

- First Prism video-to-Shorts editor for Mac.

- Gemini became the only AI pipeline for picking Shorts and framing.

- Better Shorts selection, caption customization and editing.

- Shared rendering engine with tests.

URL: https://prismclips.app/privacy
Title: Privacy — Prism

PRIVACY

# Your footage stays yours.
Plain-language summary of where your data goes. Last updated 2026-10-27.

### On your computer

- Your source video files. Prism copies them into a project and never changes the originals.

- Projects, previews and rendered MP4s.

### Sent for AI processing
Prism has no offline mode. On Mac, requests go through Prism’s server (Supabase) to OpenRouter and an AI model provider. Windows and Linux send requests directly to Google’s Gemini API using your own API key. The relevant providers’ terms apply to this data:

- Audio chunks of the part of the video you selected.

- Transcripts.

- Sampled frames: up to 12 per refinement batch, and about 1 per second of each tracked Short.

- Editor chat messages, with recent conversation and a short edit summary.
Temporary audio files are deleted after each request. The Mac server logs may include portions of model responses for diagnostics. See OpenRouter’s Privacy Policy and Terms, and Google’s Privacy Policy and Gemini API terms.

### Your Prism account
Your Prism account is stored with our database provider, Supabase. Paid plans are not available during the current beta. The account stores:

- Your email address and password. The password is stored hashed by Supabase Auth.

- Any Paddle subscription and customer IDs, status and next billing date, if associated with your account.

- One record per finished export from the Mac app: the date, number of Shorts, total length in seconds and export quality.

- One record per video you make Shorts from: a fingerprint of the file’s name and length (not the video), the day and its length in minutes.

- The total cost of your AI requests and any promo codes you redeemed, to enforce your allowance.
No video, audio, transcripts or titles are stored in your account. Database rules let each user read only their own records. Deleting your account deletes its export records.

### Questions or deletion requests
Open an issue on GitHub to ask a question or to have your account deleted.

This page describes how the software works. It is not legal advice.

Title: Terms — Prism

TERMS

# Terms of use
The short version: Prism is beta software, provided as is. Last updated 2026-10-27.

### The software
Prism is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind.

### Beta status
Prism is early beta software. Review every Short before you publish it, and keep your own backups. The Windows and Linux versions have not been tested on real devices yet.

### Your content
You keep all rights to your videos and exports. You are responsible for having the rights to the footage you process and the Shorts you publish.

### AI processing
On Mac, Prism sends audio, transcripts and sampled frames through its server to OpenRouter, which passes them to an AI model provider. Windows and Linux send requests to Google’s Gemini API using your own API key. The relevant providers’ terms apply.

### Your account
Keep your password safe and don’t use the account to break the service or access other people’s data. Accounts may be removed if they are abused. See the Privacy page for what the account stores.

### Changes
These terms may change as Prism grows. The date at the top shows the latest version.

This is a plain-language draft, not legal advice.
